This procedure - which can only be performed on a Willing Target who possesses one or more Aberrant skills - is a twenty-minute brain surgery that requires both the practitioner and Target to expend 1 Resolve. After completion, the subject's Aberrant abilities can no longer be accessed, and the Target gains 1 Fracture that is often related to the general nature of their previous abilities. Removal (not Soothing) of this Fracture causes the procedure's effects to cease.

After three attended events, the subject may unlearn all Aberrant skills and professions, regaining the XP that they had spent, and also removing the Fracture gained from the procedure.. If they choose not to do so at this time, the effects of the procedure cease and their Aberrant skills are once again available to them.
metadata.notes: Use of this procedure must be added to the character's player notes so that the date it was used can be recorded and the partial rebuild done on the correct date. Player consent should be received before using this procedure on a PC, to avoid situations where in-game coercion might create an uncomfortable situation out of game for the player.

This injectable can only be used in the process of agreeing to pay back a debt of a specified amount of currency, generally as part of an agreement when receiving a loan, and a Guide should be present to mark details on the character's sheet. The willing Target (self) is afflicted with Stage 1 Crippling Debt Disease.

CRIPPLING DEBT DISEASE
Stages of Illness: Stage 1 has no symptoms. Every additional stage (max 5) reduces the afflicted character's max Body by 10 points, to a minimum of 1. Every stage after the first comes with lack of sleep and increasing starvation-like symptoms - dark shadows under the eyes, hollow cheeks, shaky/unsteady hands.
Duration Between Stages: Crippling Debt progresses every month that at least half of the remaining debt is not paid back to the creditor.
Resolution: Full payment of the debt or the permanent death of the creditor cures Crippling Debt at any stage. Death does not cure Crippling Debt. 
Immunity: Contracting this illness and having it cured does not prevent future infection.
Special: This disease cannot be transferred or suppressed by other mechanics.

This 20 minute procedure requires two Targets - a donor and recipient, both of whom must be willing. Completion causes the donor Target to lose 1 Infection, while the recipient Target gains 1 Infection  and gain 1 Fracture. The recipient's Fracture should manifest as minor personality traits from the person donating the Infection. This procedure does not allow a person to exceed or increase their Infection Pool.
metadata.notes: Any effect which would prevent the loss of the donor's Infection from this procedure also prevents the recipient from gaining an Infection from it.
metadata.validTargetDescription: Two Lineage Targets
metadata.descriptionOfRoleplay: There are certain ways to torture someone, and this is one of the worst. Each subject is normally strapped to a table to keep them from flailing wildly. Then, both subjects have their chest cut open and their ribs cracked apart to expose their hearts. The individual conducting the procedure then removes tissue from the donor and begins transplanting it into the one receiving the Infection – pieces of heart, lung, bone, and sinew. Finally, when the trauma is greatest – which causes the Infection to be more easily removed – the donor’s skull is cracked open and their brain exposed. While the recipient heals, the donor find the inability to heal as they are cut – again and again. Many individuals who conduct this procedure find that making the trauma as terrible as they can for the donor allows for the Infection transfer to go more smoothly, since there is a link between Infection, harvesting it, and trauma.

metadata.descriptionOfRoleplay: The Nuclear Home is a term that means something much different in the post-apocalypse than it did before the Fall of humanity. The Nuclear Home is a place where individuals can come together, bond with each other and their neighborhood of faithful, and become a dedication of faith and devotion to each other. metadata.descriptionOfRoleplay: There is a secret among Gorgers – a procedure that allows them to bestow their ability to consume large amounts of fresh meat to others. A Gorger first lacerates themselves and others before sharing their blood, allowing their Infection to mingle with others. They push a knife down each person’s throat, followed by a measure of their blood. They make sure to piercing each Strain’s stomach. This procedure may Target 5 to 10 people, requires at least 5. Videbit Mortis allows players to engage echoes of dead NPCs from the local branch's history. These scenes can reveal information, provide guidance and/or tie into Local plot but cannot reveal Pre-Fall or non-Local information. The nature and mechanics of these scenes will vary and can be deadly.
metadata.notes: Requires 1 month written notice for preparation.
metadata.validTargetDescription: 5-10 Lineage Targets
metadata.descriptionOfRoleplay: Diving into the Mortis requires time, preparation, and intent if certain information is sought. First, the individual conducting the procedure must find, preferably, a biological specimen of the one they seek. This could be a sample of blood, hair, or – in a pinch – a close relation. This sample is used as an Infection-fueled focus that is combined with various other ingredients and, most importantly, concentrated Infection. This poisonous concoction is then eaten by each individual attempting the dive, and their bodies immediately collapse to the ground. Those conducting the procedure also find that doing an advance talk of the person they’re seeking, what is known about them, and what they want answered may assist in making sure the procedure goes smoothly
